title: A field-groupoid point with invertible residue maps gives translation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $(V,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ an absolute groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Let $r\in|R|$ be a point for which both induced maps $k\to\kappa(r)$ [def-weil-residue-field] from $s,t$ are isomorphisms. There are morphisms $u,v:V\to R$ with image $r$, with $s\circ u=\mathrm{id}_V$ and $t\circ v=\mathrm{id}_V$, and $t\circ u$ is an automorphism of $V$ with $v=u\circ(t\circ u)^{-1}$. The morphism $L_r:R\to R$ given on test-scheme points by $x\mapsto c(u\circ t\circ x,x)$ is a scheme automorphism, with inverse $y\mapsto c(i\circ v\circ t\circ y,y)$. It satisfies $L_r\circ e=u$, and hence sends the identity point to $r$. No finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04LS (lemma-groupoid-on-field-move-point), statement and explicit morphisms in its proof.

proof.text: Write $\alpha,\beta:k\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(r)$ for the residue maps of $s,t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] there is a canonical $j_r:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(r)\to R$ with image $r$. Set $u=j_r\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha^{-1})$ and $v=j_r\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\beta^{-1})$. Naturality [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] gives $s\circ j_r=\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ and $t\circ j_r=\operatorname{Spec}\beta$, identifying the canonical residue point of $V$ with $\mathrm{id}_V$. Thus functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $s\circ u=t\circ v=\mathrm{id}_V$, and both $u,v$ have image $r$. Put $\theta=t\circ u=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha^{-1}\circ\beta)$. It is an automorphism with inverse $\operatorname{Spec}(\beta^{-1}\circ\alpha)=s\circ v$. The same functoriality gives $v=u\circ\theta^{-1}$ and $v\circ\theta=u$; hence $u\circ s\circ v=v$.

source.place: Tag 04LS (lemma-groupoid-on-field-move-point), proof, first paragraph: construction of a,b

proof.text:
Construct actual scheme morphisms using the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]:
$L=c\circ\langle u\circ t,\mathrm{id}_R\rangle$ and $M=c\circ\langle i\circ v\circ t,\mathrm{id}_R\rangle$.
The first pair is composable because $s\circ u\circ t=t$; the second because $s\circ i\circ v\circ t=t\circ v\circ t=t$, using the groupoid identities [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. For any $x:T\to R$, precomposition gives $Lx=c(u\circ t\circ x,x)$ and $Mx=c(i\circ v\circ t\circ x,x)$ as asserted. Below juxtaposition denotes composition of scheme morphisms, with $c(a,b)$ interpreted by the fibre-product lift. We will compute the two composites at the universal $R$-point $\mathrm{id}_R$, so the resulting equalities are equalities of morphisms.

source.place: Tag 04LS (lemma-groupoid-on-field-move-point), proof, definitions of Psi and Phi and composability

proof.text:
For $q=v\circ t:R\to R$ one has $tq=t$, and the target law gives $tM=tiq=sq$. Thus $u\circ t\circ M=u\circ s\circ v\circ t=q$ by step 1. Apply associativity, the inverse law and the left unit law of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]:
$L\circ M=c(q,c(iq,\mathrm{id}_R))=c(c(q,iq),\mathrm{id}_R)=c(e\circ tq,\mathrm{id}_R)=c(e\circ t,\mathrm{id}_R)=\mathrm{id}_R$.
All compositions in this calculation are defined: $s(iq)=tq=t$ and $s(q)=t(iq)$, so the triple $(q,iq,\mathrm{id}_R)$ is composable.

source.place: Tag 04LS (lemma-groupoid-on-field-move-point), proof, first displayed inverse calculation

proof.text:
For $p=u\circ t:R\to R$ one has $sp=t$ and $tL=tp=\theta\circ t$. Consequently $v\circ t\circ L=v\circ\theta\circ t=p$ by step 1. Using the same groupoid laws [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], now in the opposite inverse identity,
$M\circ L=c(ip,c(p,\mathrm{id}_R))=c(c(ip,p),\mathrm{id}_R)=c(e\circ sp,\mathrm{id}_R)=c(e\circ t,\mathrm{id}_R)=\mathrm{id}_R$.
The triple $(ip,p,\mathrm{id}_R)$ is composable because $s(p)=t$ and $s(ip)=t(p)$. Hence $L$ is a scheme automorphism with inverse $M$, which is exactly the inverse formula in the statement.

source.place: Tag 04LS (lemma-groupoid-on-field-move-point), proof, second displayed inverse calculation

proof.text: Finally $t\circ e=\mathrm{id}_V$ and $s\circ u=\mathrm{id}_V$, so the right unit law [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] gives $L\circ e=c(u,e)=c(u,e\circ s\circ u)=u$. The unique point of $V$ maps under $u$ to $r$ by step 1, proving the claimed action on the identity point. Every construction above uses only the two residue-map isomorphisms and the groupoid laws; no finite-type hypothesis is needed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_fieldGroupoid_pointTranslation (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Scheme.{u}} (s t : R ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (e : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ R) (i : R ⟶ R) (c : pullback s t ⟶ R) (hG : IsGroupoidScheme s t e i c) (r : R) (hs : IsIso (s.residueFieldMap r)) (ht : IsIso (t.residueFieldMap r)) : ∃ (u v : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ R) (θ : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ≅ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (L : R ≅ R), (∀ z : Spec (CommRingCat.of k), u z = r) ∧ (∀ z : Spec (CommRingCat.of k), v z = r) ∧ u ≫ s = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) ∧ v ≫ t = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) ∧ u ≫ t = θ.hom ∧ v = θ.inv ≫ u ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (x : T ⟶ R), ∃ h : (x ≫ t ≫ u) ≫ s = x ≫ t, x ≫ L.hom = pullback.lift (x ≫ t ≫ u) x h ≫ c) ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (y : T ⟶ R), ∃ h : (y ≫ t ≫ v ≫ i) ≫ s = y ≫ t, y ≫ L.inv = pullback.lift (y ≫ t ≫ v ≫ i) y h ≫ c) ∧ e ≫ L.hom = u
